setup-hamiltonian-and-perturbation: Section 2, p.3, eqs 1-2: the paper assumes the Hamiltonian, the discrete nondegenerate spectrum and the t=0 perturbation H_f = H_i + O_A dz^A. Matches the value.
deformation-functions-weyl-ordering: Section 2, p.3: the paper states the deformation functions come from differentiating the Hamiltonian function and become operators by q->q^, p->p^ with Weyl ordering. Its own construction.
natural-units: Section 2, p.3: 'Throughout this paper we use natural units with hbar = 1.' A convention the paper states.
phase-space-variations-translations-only: Section 2, p.3: states it also varies the phase-space variables, and that these variations must be translations only. The 'more general than [13]' clause is a plain scope contrast, not a result.
time-reversal-assumption: Section 2, p.5-6, eqs 15 and 24: the paper says it assumes a time-reversal invariant theory and uses it to relate correlators. A stated assumption of the derivation.
fidelity-definition-and-tensor-expansion: Section 2, p.6, eqs 26-27: F := |<m'|m>| and G defined by F = 1 + (1/2) G dz dz at lowest order. The paper's own definition.
berry-curvature-definition: Section 2, p.7, eq 32 text (also Section 2.2, p.10): F = -2 Im G. The paper's own definition of the generalized Berry curvature.
generalized-oscillator-hamiltonian: Section 3, p.10, eq 51: H = (1/2)[Z p^2 + Y(pq+qp) + X q^2] with real parameters X, Y, Z. The 'fundamental' remark is the authors' wording attributed in the value. The system itself is the paper's setup.
generalized-oscillator-normal-frequency: Section 3, p.11, eq 54: omega := (XZ - Y^2)^(1/2), the normal frequency. The paper's own definition.
phase-space-block-not-configuration-spac: Section 3, p.12-13: the paper states that the integration removes all dependence on the configuration coordinates, so this metric cannot be taken as a configuration-space metric, and that it is treated as another parameter-space metric. A caveat on its own object.
parameter-metric-singular-reduce-to-2d: Section 3, p.13: the paper states the 3-parameter metric is singular (det = 0, citing [28]) and so it fixes Z = Z0 and works with the 2D metric in X, Y. The value reports the paper's own restriction, not a new result.
linear-term-hamiltonian-setup: Section 4, p.15, eq 71: H = (1/2)(Xq^2 + Y(qp+pq) + Zp^2) + Wq with parameters W, X, Y, Z. The remark that [28] used it for the classical analog is a plain mention.
linear-term-condition-and-energy-shift: Section 4, p.15, eq 72: with XZ - Y^2 > 0 the canonical transformation gives H = (1/2)(P^2 + omega^2 Q^2) - W^2 Z/(2 omega^2), same ladder operators as (54). The paper states it as its setup for Section 4.
gaussian-state-setup-real-wavefunction-b: Section 5, p.19, eq 85: the Gaussian family with sigma(l1,l2), mu(l1,l2). The Berry-zero clause is stated with its condition (real wave function) and follows at once from F = -2 Im G, so no result beyond the paper's own definitions is relied on.
scope-one-then-two-degrees-of-freedom: Section 5, p.20: 'Up to this point we have only dealt with systems of one degree of freedom', Section 6 takes two entangled particles. Stated scope.
reduced-phase-space-metric-treated-as-pa: Section 6, p.24-25, eq 114: the paper states it analyzes the reduced 2x2 matrices of each particle and 'will consider that (114) is a metric of parameter space' with coordinates {k0,k1}. Its own modelling choice.
linear-coupled-rotation-angle-parameter-: Section 7, p.26, eqs 124-127: diagonalization by a rotation through zeta in (-pi/4, pi/4), epsilon = (B-A)/C, and the paper notes R depends on the system parameters. Stated setup.
linear-coupled-coordinates-choice-and-cu: Section 7, p.28-29: the paper states it uses {B,C} as coordinates (C is the coupling parameter) and that the analytic curvature is too cumbersome to write because of zeta. A stated choice and omission. The 'carries most of the information' phrase is the authors' rationale as attributed in the value.
kaur-scope-three-questions: Section 2, p.4: 'we address three main questions in this study', (1) competences and education needs, (2) path to bridge academia and industry, (3) where to find resources. Matches the value.
kaur-method-job-data-source: Section 2, p.4: vacancy data from the Quantum Computing Report jobs database; academic and non-profit vacancies excluded; limited to quantum companies. Matches.
kaur-method-degree-experience-criteria: Section 2, p.4-5 and Section 3, p.7: evaluated the minimal qualifying degree and experience criteria; skills demand is 'beyond the scope of this paper'; the analysis focuses on degree requirements, not skills. Matches.
kaur-method-initiative-collection: Section 2, p.5: initiatives gathered through public resources, web searches, journals, community events and collaboration during 2019-2022. Matches the quote.
kaur-limit-not-exhaustive: Section 2, p.5: 'As the main limitation of our study ... we cannot argue that it is exhaustive'; a summary at time of writing. Matches.
kaur-limit-high-school-out-of-scope: Section 7, p.25 (conclusions): the detailed overview of initiatives for high school and primary school students 'falls beyond the scope of this paper'. Matches.
data-il-definition: Section 2, p.2-3: Data-IL defined as learning from new streams of an identical distribution; no new classes or considerable shift. 'Expected to be the easiest' is stated as part of the definition and is hedged as an expectation.
domain-il-definition: Section 2, p.3: Domain-IL defined with the examples given; the continuum remark and 'design choice and/or empirical decision' are in the same passage.
class-il-definition: Section 2, p.3: Class-IL defined as extending to unseen classes; 'expected to be the hardest' is stated as an expectation in the definition passage.
task-il-definition: Section 2, p.3: Task-IL defined by task identity known at inference; 'we tested the task IL scenario with new classes introduced at each task.' Matches.
contributions-stated: Section 1, p.2: the three contributions are listed as stated in the value. They state what the paper covers, not that the outcomes hold.
crc-dataset-description: Section 3.1, p.3: CRC dataset from [13], stain-normalized 224x224 patches at 20x, 136 patients, 9 tissue types as listed. Matches.
patchcam-dataset-description: Section 3.1, p.3: PatchCam from [5], 96x96 patches, normal or tumor, 400 whole-slide images at 20x, stain-normalized to match CRC. Matches.
augmented-crc-construction: Section 3.2, p.4: Domain 1 is the original CRC, Domains 2-5 simulated; each class split into 5, one split kept for Domain 1, stain unmixing then remix on the rest. Matches.
domain-2-augmentation: Section 3.2, p.4: Domain 2 eosin scale [1.75, 2.75], hematoxylin [1.5, 2.0]. Matches.
domain-3-augmentation: Section 3.2, p.4: Domain 3 decreased eosin intensity, scale [0.4, 2.75]. Matches the paper as printed.
domain-4-augmentation: Section 3.2, p.4: Domain 4 eosin hue [-0.05, -0.03], hematoxylin [0.05, 0.08]. Matches. (The discussion on p.7 calls Domain 4 'hue and saturation'; the setup list is the authoritative text.)
domain-5-augmentation: Section 3.2, p.4: Domain 5 eosin hue [0.03, 0.05], saturation eosin [1.2, 1.4], hematoxylin [1.1, 1.3]. Matches.
cl-setup-domain-il: Section 3.2, p.4-5: Domain-IL uses the 5 domains as batches, each with all 9 classes, 8700/5 = 1740 per class per domain. Matches.
cl-setup-class-il-data-il: Section 3.2, p.5: Class-IL batches hold all examples of the new classes; Data-IL batches are random with roughly equal examples per domain. Matches.
evaluation-metrics-definitions: Section 3.2, p.6: 'experience' is defined; the reported accuracies are defined; backward transfer and forward transfer are tied to past and current/future test sets. Matches.
baselines-definitions: Section 3.2, p.6: joint training (upper bound), finetuning (lower bound), plus the online baselines (A-GEM 1 epoch; CoPE mini experiences of 128 samples, 1 epoch each). Matches.
implementation-architecture-training: Section 4.1, p.6: ResNet-18 features with a nearest mean classifier, 15 epochs, batch 16, V100/A100, 3-5 repeats, SGD lr 0.1 momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.00001 after epochs 10 and 13, grid search. Matches.
domain-gap-limitation-stain-normalizatio: Section 4.1, p.7: the authors note the five domains were designed with large gaps and that smaller gaps (for example after stain normalization) would 'potentially' improve CL. It is a caveat on their own design. The improvement is a hedged expectation, not a result.
kawchak-scope-educational: Slide 2, p.2, tip 4: '100 QML code tips are discussed based on code sources including ...', 'For educational purposes: No warranty'. Matches.
kawchak-colab-assisted: Slide 5, p.5: Colab web IDE assisted by OpenAI and Stack Overflow (footnotes g, h, i: Colab, a Cirq Stack Exchange question, OpenAI), Qiskit web IDE (j, k), PennyLane in Colab (l, GeeksforGeeks), all 9/11/23. The Cirq mapping rests on footnote h and column order.
kawchak-scope-38-demos: Figure 1, p.1: 'Qiskit (1-12) / PennyLane (13-38) QML/QiML Demos Revisited'; the demo list numbers 1 to 38 and the slides show a modification each.

theory_low.reduction-to-schrodinger-form-time-integ: Section 2.2, p.9, eqs 41-46: an informal derivation step with an i-epsilon integral; not framed as a theorem, and the quotes lose the equations.
theory_low.schrodinger-form-of-generalized-qgt: Section 2.2, p.10, eq 47: derived from eq 28 and cited to [15], not framed as a theorem. The quote drops the formula, so the conditions cannot be seen in the item.
theory_low.parameter-part-equals-perturbative-form: Section 2.2, p.10, eq 48: the paper calls it 'the known result from [16, 26]'; a recovery of a cited result by restriction, not a proved result in this paper.
theory_low.recovers-provost-vallee-form: Section 2.2, p.10, eqs 49-50: a short derivation of a known identity from the cited form; not stated as a theorem. The key relation is garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.generalized-oscillator-block-diagonal-st: Section 3, p.11, eq 55: a structural statement about the computed tensor, not proved or displayed in the paper. Block matrix lost in the text layer.
theory_low.generalized-oscillator-gxy-component: Section 3, p.12, eq 60: a computed component (the expectation values (57)-(59) are shown, the integrals are not). A computed result, not a proved theorem. The printed equation is split in the text layer.
theory_low.generalized-oscillator-parameter-tensor-: Section 3, p.12, eq 61: the paper calls it 'the well-known result' and cites [19]; agreement with a cited result, with no comparison shown.

theory_low.other-fixed-parameters-same-curvature-be: Section 3, p.13, eq 66: the relation is stated 'more precisely, considering the ground state' with no proof, and the 'same curvature in every case' is asserted, not shown. The coefficient is garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.phase-space-metric-scalar-curvature-xy: Section 3, p.14, eq 68: a computed closed form; the numerator is garbled in the text layer. A calculation result, not a proved theorem.
theory_low.phase-space-curvatures-depend-on-paramet: Section 3, p.14-15, eqs 68-70, Fig 1: behavior read from computed formulas and one plot. The divergence at the transition is shown by plot, not proved. A measured/computed result.
theory_low.phase-space-curvature-vanishes-large-n: Section 3, p.14: the n -> infinity limit follows from the 1/(2n+1) factor in eqs 68-70; stated in passing, not a theorem with conditions. The Figure 1 caption quote does not show it.
theory_low.generalized-oscillator-phase-space-block: Section 3, p.12, eq 62: a computed block whose printed form is garbled in the text layer; the value cannot be checked against the quote. A calculation result.
theory_low.linear-term-metric-berry-agree-with-prio: Section 4, p.15-16: agreement with [28] is asserted, with no comparison shown. The rank-three statement is a claim about the computed matrix (75), whose entries are garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.linear-term-reduced-berry-curvature: Section 4, p.16, eq 81: a computed matrix garbled in the text layer; a calculation result.
theory_low.linear-term-determinant-divergence-phase: Section 4, p.16, eqs 79-80, Figs 2-3: the divergence is read from a plot and formula; 'implying a phase transition' is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.linear-term-christoffel-and-ricci-report: Section 4, p.17-18: long lists of computed symbols, garbled in the text layer, with no derivation shown. A calculation result.
theory_low.linear-term-scalar-curvature-formula: Section 4, p.18, eq 82: a computed closed form, garbled in the text layer. A calculation result.
theory_low.linear-term-curvature-omega-limit-coordi: Section 4, p.18: a limit of eq 82 (R -> -4/b_n) and the authors' interpretation ('coordinate dependent'). Not a proved theorem.
theory_low.linear-term-curvature-vanishes-at-large-: Section 4, p.18-19, eq 83, Fig 4: a limit read from eq 82 and one plot; stated, not proved.
theory_low.linear-term-curvature-w-zero-and-ground-: Section 4, p.18-19, eq 84, Fig 5: limits of the computed curvature read from the formula and a plot (minimum -28 at W=0). Computed results.

theory_low.phase-space-metric-blind-to-linear-term: Section 4, p.18: stated without displaying the computation; the authors' result. Not a proved theorem.
theory_low.gaussian-state-metric-provost-vallee: Section 5, p.20, eqs 86-87: a computed metric from the Provost-Vallee form; the determinant is garbled in the text layer. A calculation.

theory_low.gaussian-state-special-case-of-linear-te: Section 5, p.20, eqs 92-93: an identification (sigma = X^(-1/4), mu = W/X) with the reduction asserted, not displayed.

theory_low.symmetric-coupled-christoffel-independen: Section 6, p.21-22: a computed list of symbols and a remark on the m, n dependence. The symbols are partly garbled; a calculation.
theory_low.symmetric-coupled-parameter-space-flat: Section 6, p.22, eq 101: Riemann tensor stated to vanish, with no intermediate steps shown. A computed result.
theory_low.symmetric-coupled-flat-coordinates-beltr: Section 6, p.22, eqs 102-106: the coordinate construction is given by the result of Beltrami's equation, not shown to be solved; equations garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.symmetric-coupled-phase-space-block-meth: Section 6, p.22-23: a method remark inside a derivation; the resulting matrix (107) is garbled in the text layer. Not a theorem.

theory_low.symmetric-coupled-entropy-behavior: Section 6, p.23-24, eqs 112-113, Fig 7: behavior read from the computed entropy and a plot; 'reducing the self coupling increases the entanglement' is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.tensor-holds-covariance-information-clai: Section 6, p.24: a conclusion drawn from one worked example (two coupled Gaussian oscillators). The general link to the covariance matrix rests on eqs 34-36 cited from [15]. An authors' claim.
theory_low.reduced-phase-space-curvature-general-fo: Section 6, p.25, eq 115: a computed closed form, numerator garbled in the text layer. A calculation.
theory_low.reduced-phase-space-curvature-limits-vs-: Section 6, p.25, eqs 116-119: limits listed without derivation. Computed results.
theory_low.reduced-phase-space-curvature-ground-sta: Section 6, p.25, eq 120, Fig 8: a computed closed form, garbled in the text layer, and a plot comparison. A calculation.
theory_low.linear-coupled-metric-excited-states-gen: Section 7, p.27, eqs 128-130: a computed metric; the generalization of [17] is asserted. Matrices garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.linear-coupled-determinant-divergence: Section 7, p.27, eq 131: a statement about the computed determinant, which is garbled in the text layer. A calculation.
theory_low.linear-coupled-ground-state-scalar-curva: Section 7, p.27-28, eq 133: R = -8 is reported with the Riemann tensor deliberately not shown ('long and uninstructive'), and under the extra assumption eps/|eps| = +1. Not a proved result.
theory_low.linear-coupled-excited-curvature-no-dive: Section 7, p.28, eq 134: a computed closed form, garbled in the text layer; 'no divergences for real values of its parameters' is asserted, not proved.
theory_low.linear-coupled-phase-space-block-reduced: Section 7, p.28, eqs 135-139: a computed block and its reduction; matrices garbled in the text layer. A calculation.
theory_low.linear-coupled-ground-state-purity-entro: Section 7, p.29, eqs 140-141: computed ground-state purity and entropy, garbled in the text layer. A calculation.
theory_low.linear-coupled-curvature-diverges-when-p: Section 7, p.29, Fig 9: an observation from one plot of the ground state; 'can recognize the maximum entanglement as a phase transition' is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.conclusion-symmetric-coupled-transition-: Section 8, p.30: a summary of computed behavior with the authors' interpretation (a normal mode becomes a free particle).
theory_low.conclusion-reduced-curvature-differs-fro: Section 8, p.30: the authors' summary and a flagged open question ('must be studied in more detail'), resting on the limits of eqs 116-119.
theory_low.conclusion-equivalence-with-prior-forms: Section 8, p.30: the authors' claim of proof and of agreement 'for every system'.
